original.target_description: Study 1: numeracy (median split) by positive/negative attribute framing interaction on ratings of five students’ examination performance; repeated-measures ANOVA.

n.sample_role: Participants in Study 1; N=100 is consistent with target four-cell ANOVA residual df=96.
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for Study 1; TV is an OCR rendering of N.

es.quote: The interaction of numeracy with frame, however, was significant, F(l, 96) = 5.6, p < .05, r\ = .11.

p.quote: The interaction of numeracy with frame, however, was significant, F(l, 96) = 5.6, p < .05

replication.target_description: Study 1, full-sample main replication: original numeracy scale dichotomized at median; numeracy by positive/negative framing interaction on exam performance ratings, mixed ANOVA; p. 11 and Table 9.

n.quote: We recruited 919 participants, but 59 of them failed the verifications or consent at the beginning. | Therefore, we had 860 participants | Therefore, we focus our analyses on the full sample.
n.sample_role: US American MTurk participants; authors report full-sample N=860. Exact analytic n for the target mixed ANOVA is not separately printed and residual df=855 is not reconciled with that N.
n.exclusions: 59 failed initial verification/consent and were filtered out. Main analyses explicitly used the full 860-person sample without the further preregistered exclusions; post-exclusion analyses are supplementary.

es.location: p. 11, Replication: Dichotomized numeracy; Table 9, p. 12
es.quote: In Study 1, we performed a mixed ANOVA and found an interaction effect of numeracy on framing effect (F(1, 855) = 5.02, p = .025, η2p = 0.01, 90% CI [0.00, 0.02])

p.location: p. 11, Replication: Dichotomized numeracy; Table 9, p. 12
p.quote: interaction effect of numeracy on framing effect (F(1, 855) = 5.02, p = .025, η2p = 0.01, 90% CI [0.00, 0.02])

reported_success.location: p. 11, Replication: Dichotomized numeracy, Study 1 paragraph
reported_success.quote: We concluded support for the hypothesis that the less numerate show a stronger framing effect than the highly numerate, with weaker effects.

notes: Both retrieved titles match the supplied references. Replication source is the published 2023 full manuscript deposited in the supplied OSF project (the input cites the 2022 OSF reference). Original text OCR corrupts N and η²; printed values retained without recalculation. Replication narrative and Table 9 agree on F=5.02, p=.025, partial eta-squared=0.01; supplementary Table S18 instead prints F=4.42 alongside the same p/effect size. Main-text target used. Replication full-sample N=860 is documented, but exact target analytic n is left null because the printed target residual df=855 is not reconciled and no separate test-specific n is printed. No metrics converted.
